title: perf(utils): precompile the wheel project-name pattern
head: d2ac6ba3f819cb5c81d79f4820db205d6f8bc126

families.why: The change replaces an inline `re.match` call with a pre‑compiled regular expression (`_wheel_name_regex`). For typical, well‑formed wheel filenames the compiled regex avoids repeated pattern compilation and cache lookup, so the new version should be faster.
families.size_meaning: n = number of allowed characters in the project‑name part of the wheel filename (the part before the first dash).
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # Build a project name consisting of n ASCII letters/digits/underscores/dots.
    # The name must not contain "__" and must match the wheel name regex.
    allowed = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_."
    # Ensure at least one character and no "__" sequence.
    name = ''.join(allowed[i % len(allowed)] for i in range(max(1, n)))
    # Avoid "__" by replacing any occurrence.
    name = name.replace('__', '_')
    # Construct a minimal valid wheel filename: name-version-py3-none-any.whl
    wheel = f"{name}-1.0-py3-none-any.whl"
    return [[wheel]]

families.why: The change pre‑compiles the wheel‑name validation regex (`_wheel_name_regex`). For valid wheel filenames the regex is executed on every call, so a longer project‑name part makes the match work harder. The head version avoids re‑compiling the pattern on each call, giving a measurable speed‑up that grows with the length of the name.
families.size_meaning: n ≈ length of the project‑name segment (number of extra ASCII word characters).
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # Build a valid wheel filename whose name part grows with n.
    # Format: {name}-{version}-{pyver}-{abi}-{platform}.whl  (4 dashes)
    name = "pkg" + "a" * n          # only word characters, no '__'
    version = "1.0"
    tag = "py3-none-any"
    filename = f"{name}-{version}-{tag}.whl"
    return [(filename,)]

def make(n):
    """Return up to 8 wheel filenames; n controls how many are produced."""
    n = min(max(n, 1), 8)
    result = []
    for i in range(n):
        # Vary the project name length to exercise the regex on different input sizes
        name = 'pkg' + 'a' * (i + 1)
        filename = f'{name}-1.0-py3-none-any.whl'
        result.append([filename])
    return result

families.family: Both the old and the new code run the same regular‑expression engine over the entire project‑name string. If the name part is extremely long and contains many U
families.why: Both the old and the new code run the same regular‑expression engine over the entire project‑name string. If the name part is extremely long and contains many Unicode word characters, the regex match will scan the whole string, and the overhead of the Python function call to the compiled regex object (`_wheel_name_regex.match`) may be marginally higher than the single `re.match` call that also compiles (or reuses a cached pattern). In practice the difference is tiny, but this family exercises the worst‑case path for the new code.
families.size_meaning: n = length of the Unicode project‑name part (number of characters).
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # Use a Unicode word character outside ASCII to force the UNICODE flag path.
    # U+03B1 (Greek small letter beta) is a word character.
    ch = chr(0x03B1)
    name = ch * max(1, n)          # e.g. βββ…
    # Ensure no "__" sequence.
    wheel = f"{name}-1.0-py3-none-any.whl"
    return [[wheel]]

families.why: Both versions use the same Unicode‑aware regex, but the head version accesses a module‑level compiled object (`_wheel_name_regex.match`) while the base version calls `re.match` each time. For inputs that force the regex engine to scan a long Unicode string before succeeding (e.g., many non‑ASCII word characters), the extra global‑lookup and method call could add a tiny constant overhead, making the head version marginally slower on this specific family.
families.size_meaning: n ≈ number of Unicode word characters (e.g., accented letters) in the project name.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # Use a Unicode letter that is a word character but not ASCII.
    ch = "\u00e9"   # 'é'
    name = "pkg" + ch * n
    version = "1.0"
    tag = "py3-none-any"
    filename = f"{name}-{version}-{tag}.whl"
    return [(filename,)]

def make(n):
    """Return up to 8 invalid wheel filenames containing '__'."""
    n = min(max(n, 1), 8)
    result = []
    for i in range(n):
        name = 'pkg__' + 'b' * i
        filename = f'{name}-1.0-py3-none-any.whl'
        result.append([filename])
    return result
